chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who comes to his wife during the obliteration (of the moon at the end of) the month, so he would not be safe from the miscarriage of the child.

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: His wife; referring to the spouse in the context of marital relations.
key_terms.لِسِقْطِ الْوَلَدِ: Safe from the miscarriage of the child; indicating a risk of miscarriage.
key_terms.مُحَاقِ الشَّهْرِ: The obliteration of the moon; the last few days of the lunar month when the moon is not visible.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marital intimacy during the last days of the lunar month when the moon is not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links marital intimacy during 'muhāq' (the new moon phase) to the potential miscarriage of the fetus, reflecting the Shia tradition of connecting physical acts with cosmic influences. It underscores the concept of 'tathir' (purification) and the spiritual-physical harmony in family life, where specific timings are believed to affect progeny's health and vitality.
